_comment: Cached output of prompts/attendee.md — one `claude -p` call per event, reused for every attendee regardless of list size. --live regenerates this file; offline mode reads it as-is. Every quote is timestamp-attributable to data/incoming/transcript.md.

marketing.headline: Subject lines aren't a rounding error.
marketing.body: Daniel Kim (Northwind Analytics) A/B tested two attendee thank-you subject lines — one led with the speaker's name, one led with a specific stat — and the stat-led version won by about 14 percentage points on open rate. [18:15]

revops.headline: Multi-threading is already happening — most teams just don't see it.
revops.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) flagged that accounts with three or more attendees on the same webinar convert to opportunity at almost double the rate of single-attendee accounts — worth checking your own account list for this event. [25:04]

sales.headline: Context wins the first call.
sales.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) described hot-attendee tasks getting routed to reps with real context attached — e.g. "attended the full session, asked about integration timelines" — rather than a bare list. That context is what changes how a rep opens the conversation. [13:50]

executive.headline: The number that gets budget approved.
executive.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) shared a directional range of 11–14x return on fully-loaded event cost within two quarters, counting both direct and repurposed-content pipeline — though she was clear it's a mature-program number, not a first-event expectation. [51:48]

customer_success.headline: Every draft still gets a human set of eyes.
customer_success.body: Daniel Kim (Northwind Analytics) was explicit in Q&A: "AI drafts, human approves, every single time" — no generated follow-up or repurposed asset goes out unreviewed. [58:28]

general.headline: Segmentation alone triples click-through.
general.body: Sara Alvarez (Meridian Software) shared that moving from one blanket post-webinar email to attendee/no-show/speaker segmentation — plus role-based variants — took overall click-through from about 6% to just over 17%, without changing send timing at all. [28:20]

by_industry.saas: Daniel Kim's point about a fourth personalization layer, industry and company size, is worth applying literally here: he described leading enterprise-tier takeaways with integration and security rather than pricing, since that's usually the actual blocker on a software deal. [26:52]
by_industry.services_it: If you're reading this from an IT-services or agency seat, Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]) is the reason this doesn't read like a generic recap — the same transcript is meant to land differently depending on which of your own client accounts it's relevant to.
by_industry.other_commercial: Per Daniel Kim's fourth-layer point ([26:15]), the version of this worth your attention outside pure enterprise software leads with time-to-value and pricing rather than integration depth — that's the objection he flagged as the real one at smaller or less software-native shops. [26:52]
